before_body:
Matching family Christmas sweaters can bring a holiday card, a school event and a party outfit together. Start with your family's plans: the earliest occasion you'll wear them, the people joining in and whether you'd like a bold festive picture or a repeating winter pattern.

For Christmas 2026, use this guide to compare designs, work through everyone's sizes and plan around estimated delivery. Each piece is sold separately, so you can build your family's outfits one person at a time.

How to choose a style

Choose a color to anchor the group: try red with simple dark trousers, green with denim, or navy with cream accessories. Then decide between a central picture and a repeating pattern. For a school event, check any clothing guidance before choosing accessories.

Santa designs: decorating scenes and cheerful lettering

Two green options take different approaches. Jingle Bells Santa sweaters feature a waving Santa beneath white lettering, with red ornaments and a stocking framed by bell and snowflake bands. Ho Ho Santa sweaters repeat Santa faces, white HO! lettering and snowflakes across deep green. Choose the first for a central scene or the second for a repeating motif.

For red, Santa Tree Delivery sweaters show Santa carrying a decorated tree and holding a gift, with green trim and snowflake-pattern sleeves. Santa Tree Topper sweaters show him on a ladder placing a gold star on a tree, with white cuffs and a white hem band. Try either for a tree-decorating photo.

Reindeer designs: a face or a festive scene

Santa Hat Reindeer sweaters place a smiling cream reindeer face, black antlers and a red Santa hat against bright red and white snowflakes. Candy Cane Reindeer sweaters add a red-and-white candy cane, with snowflake bands and zigzag rows framing the reindeer. Both give you a central character to keep visible when arranging a group portrait.

Nordic and snowflake jacquard: rows of winter details

For a patterned look, Nordic Reindeer sweaters combine white reindeer and snowflakes on red with navy bands and small trees. Nordic Heart Reindeer sweaters use deep navy, a cream band of reindeer faces, little brown hearts, white trees and geometric rows.

Reindeer Row sweaters place tan reindeer across a white chest above a navy lower body, with dots and a zigzag below. For another red option, Christmas Reindeer sweaters combine a green chest band of red reindeer and white trees with more reindeer, trees and snowflake dots below. Keep trousers or skirts plain to let these patterns lead.

Polar bears: a different winter animal

Polar Bear Christmas sweaters show white bears in Santa hats and scarves beside a green tree and wrapped gifts, with white snowflakes on bright red. Consider this design if your family would enjoy an animal theme beyond reindeer; its child labels also reach older ages, as explained below.

Stockings and string lights: decorating details

Christmas Stocking sweaters scatter red stockings with white cuffs and white snowflakes across deep green. Reindeer String Lights sweaters show a scarf-wearing reindeer on navy, with red, green and white lights around its antlers. The lights are part of the knit pattern, with no electronics.

Sizing the whole family

Choose one piece per person, selecting the role and size for each wearer. Adult sizes are unisex, so mom and dad choose from the same adult range. Kids choose child sizes by age, then check the measurements rather than relying on the age label alone.

Eleven designs list Child 2 Years, 3 Years, 4 Years, 5 Years and 6–7 Years. The exceptions are Polar Bear Christmas and Christmas Reindeer, which list Child 4–5, 6–7, 8–9 and 10–12 Years. These two also use paired adult labels: S/M through XL/2XL for the polar bear design, and S-M through XL-2XL for the reindeer design.

Across the other designs, adult ranges start at either XXS or S and run through 3XL. Check your chosen page before assembling the order; the same size label should not replace a measurement check.

Open “Size guide & fit” on each product page for garment measurements in cm and inches. Lay a favorite well-fitting sweater flat and compare it with the chart, following the measuring points shown. Record each person's results, including room for any planned layer underneath. Read the 30-day returns policy as part of your buying decision.

When to order for Christmas

Standard shipping is included on orders. Each product page shows estimated delivery, currently about 12–16 days after ordering. Check the date on the product page when you order, especially if you need the sweaters for an early school event, party or holiday card session.

For US orders, the product pages currently estimate delivery before Christmas for orders placed by December 8. This is only an estimate, so no arrival date is promised. Plan around your first wearing date and leave extra time for trying everything on and arranging photos. A Christmas delivery estimate may be too late for your card-making plans.

Photo ideas for your Christmas card

  • Keep the background simple. Try a plain wall or an uncluttered corner beside the tree so the sweater designs remain easy to see.
  • Check the light first. Take a test picture near a window before gathering everyone, and adjust your position if faces look shadowed.
  • Show the sweater fronts. Arrange hands and props below the main picture or chest band; check that one person's shoulder isn't hiding another's design.
  • Photograph a small activity. Hang an ornament or gather around a wrapped gift, then take a simple group portrait. Leave space around the family for cropping or card text.

Compare matching family Christmas sweaters with your family's sizes and first event in mind. For Christmas morning, explore matching family Christmas pajamas and use the matching family Christmas pajamas guide to plan that part of your holiday wardrobe.
